# Control map

<!-- Generated by tools/governance.py --write; edit control-registry.json. -->

This is an implemented control inventory, not a test-run report.
Review on changed standards, mechanisms, evidence or coverage. The
[registry](control-registry.json) owns these mappings; [engineering](engineering.md)
owns mandatory wording and [charter](charter.md) owns principles.

Automatic controls run in the common lane. Runtime controls act in the live system;
their tests cover only the stated cases. Manual controls require the named review
or probe. Implementation and evidence links do not assert a current execution or pass.

## Mechanisms and coverage

### C-PORTABLE — Portable regression lane (automatic)

Controller, HTTP adapter, setup and spectator regressions. Includes gameplay record validation and bounded evidence retention using synthetic observations. Common command compiles Python, runs selected Ruff correctness diagnostics, Import Linter contracts, JavaScript syntax checks, Python tests and delayed-image viewer tests; markdown-it-py parses document links/images before contained file-target checks; diff whitespace is checked.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: each integration checkpoint and configured CI event.
Enforcement: Common command and opt-in local hook; main also requires the observed GitHub Actions controller check (app 15368) with strict freshness under active ruleset 25319489. Local hooks remain bypassable; dated hosted/probe evidence is in public-workflow acceptance.
Failure response: Preserve failure output, fix the cause and rerun before claiming portable acceptance.

Evidence / implementation: [tools/check.py](../tools/check.py), [tests/test_controller.py](../tests/test_controller.py), [tests/test_server.py](../tests/test_server.py), [tests/test_setup.py](../tests/test_setup.py), [tests/test_viewer.cjs](../tests/test_viewer.cjs), [.github/workflows/check.yml](../.github/workflows/check.yml), [.githooks/pre-commit](../.githooks/pre-commit), [pyproject.toml](../pyproject.toml), [requirements-dev.lock](../requirements-dev.lock), [tests/test_devtools.py](../tests/test_devtools.py), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md), [tests/test_gameplay_contracts.py](../tests/test_gameplay_contracts.py), [tests/test_gameplay_evidence.py](../tests/test_gameplay_evidence.py), [tests/test_cli.py](../tests/test_cli.py), [tests/test_gameplay_memory.py](../tests/test_gameplay_memory.py).

Coverage gap: Fake bridge tests do not execute CDDA. Loopback tests require bind permission; missing Node or dev tools and denied binds fail the lane. Markdown link/image targets are checked, excluding anchors, external availability and raw HTML links. Ruff selects E9/F63/F7/F82, not comprehensive formatting or typing.

### C-RUNTIME — Live authority and input guards (runtime)

Single-controller dispatch, HTTP trust boundary and spectator input freshness. Controller serializes each channel, persists separate gameplay/control admissions and revokes durable host tokens before retirement; native v3 checks boundary, matching frame, expiry and token at input commit. Recovery is limited to owned native interruption queries and one raw debug Space. Server validates origin/token/frame paths and rejects recovery ingress; viewer waits for matching decoded image and supported ordinary boundary.

Owner: controller and viewer maintainer. Trigger: every relevant request, observation and image decode.
Enforcement: Implemented at runtime; regression execution is C-PORTABLE. Source references alone establish no behavioral pass.
Failure response: Reject or freeze further dispatch; expose error and reconcile by observation before explicit resume.

Evidence / implementation: [harness/controller.py](../harness/controller.py), [harness/server.py](../harness/server.py), [web/app.js](../web/app.js), [tests/test_controller.py](../tests/test_controller.py), [tests/test_server.py](../tests/test_server.py), [tests/test_viewer.cjs](../tests/test_viewer.cjs), [docs/protocol.md](../docs/protocol.md), [native/cdda_harness.cpp](../native/cdda_harness.cpp), [harness/gameplay/evidence.py](../harness/gameplay/evidence.py).

Coverage gap: Tests exercise fake-bridge and browser fixtures. Native takeover and engine input behavior need C-NATIVE. Pause cannot cancel an already-running activity; no structured damage/trap or combat guarantee.

### C-BOUNDARY — Architectural dependency contracts (automatic)

Declared controller and server dependency boundaries, including indirect imports through harness modules. Passive gameplay records and evidence must not import controller, HTTP, CLI or process/build tooling. Import Linter uses the pyproject.toml forbidden contracts: controller cannot depend on server, CLI, declared network modules or build tooling; server cannot depend on CLI/tools; CLI may compose both.

Owner: harness maintainer. Trigger: common command; architecture changes require rule review.
Enforcement: Common command runs the real lint-imports executable and propagates failure; temporary source fixtures exercise allowed composition and direct/indirect forbidden imports.
Failure response: Remove reversed dependency or review the boundary and checker together before accepting changed architecture.

Evidence / implementation: [pyproject.toml](../pyproject.toml), [tools/check.py](../tools/check.py), [tests/test_devtools.py](../tests/test_devtools.py), [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), [docs/decisions/003-development-controls.md](../docs/decisions/003-development-controls.md).

Coverage gap: Static import graph with configured external roots. Dynamic imports, external-package internals, undeclared libraries and semantic C++ isolation remain review concerns; this is not comprehensive module layering.

Lifecycle: active. Rationale: none recorded. Replacement: none.

Last exercise: 2026-10-17. Outcome: Passed within recorded scope after preserved repairs; limitations retained.
Scope: Three Import Linter contracts, adding passive gameplay and negative import fixtures.

### C-REVIEW — Design and independent change review (manual)

Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions. Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance.

Owner: lead; reviewer supplies independent findings. Trigger: significant change, new boundary/guarantee/dependency or integration checkpoint.
Enforcement: Required by S-AGENT and the GitHub work/PR workflow; independent agent review is manually recorded, not an independent GitHub human approval. Hosted enforcement is recorded separately in acceptance.
Failure response: Resolve material findings or record scoped owner/reason/revisit exception; after two unsuccessful worker repairs lead takes back the work.

### C-GOVERNANCE — Registry, evidence schema and map validation (automatic)

Standard mappings, control lifecycle/maintenance, document stewardship, local references, curated manifest metadata and generated map. Existing jsonschema validates records and YAML metadata parsed by python-frontmatter; project checks enforce current lifecycle relationships, safe references, active-only mappings, due dates, protocol source agreement and generated-map freshness. --as-of explicitly forecasts maintenance; the common command evaluates today.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: common command; regenerate map after registry change.
Enforcement: Common command fails; negative tests exercise mapping/field/reference/drift failures. Normal mode never rewrites the map.
Failure response: Fix missing/unknown mappings, unsafe references or metadata; regenerate stale map with --write and inspect the result.

### C-PROTOCOL — Protocol v3 source agreement (automatic)

Native emitter/validator, controller send/response/stored-request validators, server advertisement, CLI discovery validator, viewer guard and protocol document version. Recognize current native observation/control emitters and validators, Python AST request/response literals for both channels, discovery, viewer, evidence schema and document version; require v3 in every bounded source form. Representation changes require checker review.

Owner: bridge and controller maintainer. Trigger: common command; any protocol representation change requires checker review.
Enforcement: Common command fails on version drift or unrecognized source form; each representation has a negative fixture.
Failure response: Resolve version drift; for a refactor/version change review and update checker plus contract, then run required native acceptance.

Coverage gap: Narrow source drift detector, not a robust C++ parser or protocol conformance proof. Refactored representations fail for review; matching literals cannot prove runtime behavior.

Enforcement: Implemented stage guards plus portable setup regressions; native reproducibility requires C-NATIVE and manual provenance review.
Failure response: Stop failed stage, preserve diagnostics and retry only after identifying the corrupt input or owned workspace.

### C-RELEASE — Exact candidate and evidence review (manual)

Checkpoint/release scope, source provenance and validation lanes. Inspect staged diff and candidate identity, run common checks against exact candidate, review pins/open exceptions and require relevant native probes for affected claims.

Owner: lead or releasing maintainer. Trigger: checkpoint, release or support claim.
Enforcement: Main requires a PR, the Actions-bound controller check and resolved conversations; no force-push/deletion or configured bypass. Lead still owns native/release acceptance. Zero required human approvals is an explicit single-account limit; agent review is not human approval.
Failure response: Hold the affected acceptance/release claim until failed or unexecuted required lanes are resolved or scope is explicitly reduced.

Evidence / implementation: [docs/setup.md#evidence-and-releases](../docs/setup.md#evidence-and-releases), [docs/engineering.md](../docs/engineering.md), [docs/runbook.md#native-acceptance-lane](../docs/runbook.md#native-acceptance-lane), [native/upstream.json](../native/upstream.json), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md).

Coverage gap: Working-tree hooks do not prove a partially staged candidate. Hosted source/check enforcement does not establish native gameplay, semantic review or release authority. No tag or release automation is installed; administrators can later change rules.

### C-MAINTENANCE — Drift, recovery and retention review (manual)

Active guidance, dependency/research freshness, failure evidence and project-owned cleanup. Review active guidance/visuals, controls and dependencies on changed behavior/failure/release/resumption and within recorded periodic dates. Record findings, effectiveness, cost and follow-up in registry with dated evidence; promote repeated defects into tests or revise/retire controls. C-GOVERNANCE detects elapsed due dates when invoked.

Owner: maintainer; lead tracks active work. Trigger: behavior/control failure, release, resumed work or active-development review interval.
Enforcement: Manual requirements under S-OPS/S-AGENT/S-DOCS/S-EVIDENCE, with registry fields, references and overdue dates enforced by C-GOVERNANCE in the common lane.
Failure response: Record specific owner and next action, repair inaccurate guidance and preserve unresolved failures; never delete saves as routine cleanup.

Evidence / implementation: [docs/work.md](../docs/work.md), [docs/runbook.md](../docs/runbook.md), [docs/research-engineering.md](../docs/research-engineering.md), [docs/research.md](../docs/research.md), [docs/environment.md](../docs/environment.md).

Coverage gap: Review quality and event-trigger detection remain manual. No background scheduler, automatic drift measurement or deletion job; passing date checks proves only that recorded dates are not overdue, not that review occurred.

Lifecycle: active. Rationale: none recorded. Replacement: none.

Last exercise: 2026-10-17. Outcome: Passed within recorded scope after preserved repairs; limitations retained.
Scope: Behavior-triggered current guidance/control review, incident retention and owned runtime cleanup.
Exercise evidence: [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-recovery-memory.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-recovery-memory.md).

Findings: Current docs and scopes updated to v3 and passive memory; prior reports remain history. Native/semantic failures preserved and repaired without weakening guards. Long-term effectiveness remains unmeasured.
Cost: Targeted independent review, existing common checks and serialized native probes; manual acceptance remains substantial.
Follow-up: Review on relevant contract/failure/release or recorded due date. #31 public controls, #8 broad recovery, #33 gameplay evidence and #13 maintenance remain separate work.

### C-VISUAL — Rendered visual documentation (automatic)

Mermaid sources and generated SVGs in docs/diagrams. Pinned local Mermaid CLI renders every source in a headless project-local browser. Hash receipt covers sources, config, wrapper, package lock and tracked SVGs; title/description and root SVG ID are required. Explicit --write regenerates; normal checks leave tracked files unchanged.

Owner: documentation maintainer. Trigger: common command; source, renderer configuration or dependency changes require rendered review.
Enforcement: Common command fails on renderer errors, missing title/description/ID or changed input/output receipts; negative fixtures include a real parse failure. No global installation or automatic fetch.
Failure response: Fix syntax or missing setup; regenerate stale output and inspect the rendered result. Never call a denied browser launch a passed check. Resolve semantic/readability findings through C-USABILITY/C-REVIEW.

Evidence / implementation: [tools/diagrams.py](../tools/diagrams.py), [tests/test_diagrams.py](../tests/test_diagrams.py), [docs/diagrams/rendered.json](../docs/diagrams/rendered.json), [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), [docs/overview.md](../docs/overview.md), [package.json](../package.json), [package-lock.json](../package-lock.json), [.puppeteerrc.cjs](../.puppeteerrc.cjs), [docs/decisions/004-documentation-controls.md](../docs/decisions/004-documentation-controls.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-public-workflow.md).

Coverage gap: Receipt freshness is not cross-host byte equality or proof against deliberate falsification. Rendering and SVG metadata do not prove meaning, accessibility for every reader or readable layout. Human rendered inspection is required. Ubuntu 24.04 CI was exercised with a scoped runner Chrome sandbox profile; other Linux hosts remain unverified.

Lifecycle: active. Rationale: Required to keep user-facing visual explanations reviewable and synchronized.. Replacement: none.

Last exercise: 2026-10-17. Outcome: Passed within recorded scope after preserved repairs; limitations retained.
Scope: Current Python recovery flow rendered and inspected at ordinary width, independently compared with the current contract.
Exercise evidence: [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-recovery-memory.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-recovery-memory.md).

Cost: Targeted independent review, existing common checks and serialized native probes; manual acceptance remains substantial.

## Interpreting results

Run `.venv/bin/python tools/check.py` for the portable lane; update this map with
`.venv/bin/python tools/governance.py --write`. The latter validates before writing and
does not run gameplay. Dated executions belong in [acceptance](acceptance/2026-10-17-mvp.md)
and [work](work.md), with exact candidate, failures and unexecuted lanes.
